How does SCRIPE-Backend enforce 5-layer zero-trust security and multi-DB tenant isolation?

Long image

A

Answer

SCRIPE-Backend enforces a 29-stage ordered HTTP middleware gate, fail-closed Redis JWT revocation, expression-tree tenant query filters, and Dual-Mode persistence across PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and Oracle.1

  1. Every mutating request must clear Cloudflare origin verification, rate limits, JWT revocation, CSRF, replay nonce, and PBAC before entering AstraFlow.2
  2. BaseDbContext compiles expression-tree global filters for TenantId and !IsDeleted on every entity while stamping UTC audit trails.3
  3. AddModuleMultiProviderDatabase resolves each module's DbContext to either the shared physical database (Mode 1) or a dedicated module database (Mode 2) while preserving isolated schemas.4
  4. Sensitive PII and idempotency receipt payloads are encrypted with AES-GCM and external IDs are obfuscated via ScripeSecureIdCodec.5

Applies to29-Stage HTTP GatePBAC (RBAC+GBAC+ABAC)AES-GCMPostgreSQL / SQL Server / Oracle

How are the 5 defense layers and Dual-Mode schemas wired across the backend host?

Diagram structure
  • Clients & Edge client
  • JWT & Revocation identity_auth
  • Middleware Pipeline http_pipeline
  • OTel & Real-Time observability
  • API Controllers controllers
  • Redis L1 & Locks redis_cache
  • AstraFlow Mediator mediator
  • EventBus & Inbox event_bus
  • 18 Domain Modules handlers
  • CatalogPricing Engine pricing_engine
  • BaseDbContext base_dbcontext
  • OutboxProcessorJob outbox_processor
  • Schema-Isolated DBs module_db
  • client → http_pipeline · HTTPS
  • http_pipeline → identity_auth · verify JWT
  • http_pipeline → observability · traces & hubs
  • http_pipeline → controllers · PBAC route
  • controllers → mediator · ISender.Send
  • mediator → redis_cache · L1 cache & lock
  • mediator → handlers · dispatch
  • handlers → pricing_engine · Quote Contract
  • handlers → base_dbcontext · SaveChanges
  • pricing_engine → base_dbcontext · Freeze Quote
  • base_dbcontext → module_db · atomic commit
  • module_db → outbox_processor · poll outbox
  • outbox_processor → event_bus · publish batch
  • event_bus → mediator · INotification
Layer 1: Network & Ingress
TLS 1.3, ForwardedHeaders, Cloudflare origin guard, strict CORS, and per-user/login/global rate limiting
Layer 2: Authentication
15-minute access JWT + 30-day httpOnly refresh cookie + fail-closed Redis IAccountRevocationCache
Layer 3: Authorization (PBAC)
Declarative [PermissionRequired] combining RBAC roles, GBAC groups, and ABAC resource policies
Layer 4: Data & Tenant Isolation
Expression-tree TenantId query filters, AES-GCM PII encryption, and ScripeSecureIdCodec opaque IDs
Layer 5: Immutable Audit
Automatic before/after JSON field diffs written to core.audit_logs inside BaseDbContext.SaveChangesAsync
2

How does the 29-stage security gate validate and authorize a mutating request?

Diagram structure
  • API Caller client
  • MiddlewarePipeline mw
  • Redis Revocation/Nonce redis
  • PBAC Auth Handler pbac
  • BaseDbContext db
  • client → mw · POST /api/v1/venue/reservations (JWT + CSRF + Nonce)
  • mw → redis · Check IAccountRevocationCache & Replay Nonce
  • redis → mw · Token Active & Nonce Fresh
  • mw → pbac · Evaluate [PermissionRequired] + Tenant Claim
  • pbac → mw · Policy Granted
  • mw → db · Execute Handler -> SaveChangesAsync (TenantId == Current)
  • db → client · 200 OK Result<T> (Sensitive Fields Redacted)

Fail-Closed Account Revocation & Cross-Tenant Guard

If a user's role or session is revoked, IAccountRevocationCache immediately blocks active 15-minute JWTs before they expire. At the data layer, BaseDbContext rejects any entity mutation whose TenantId mismatches the authenticated ICurrentUser.TenantId.6
